attribution.citationTitle: Penn AI Guidance and Policies
attribution.sourceRights: Tracker metadata is open licensed. Official source documents, page text, PDFs, and other source materials retain their original rights and terms.

claims.claimText: Users of AI at Penn are accountable for AI-generated content and should validate its accuracy with trusted first-party sources, being wary of misinformation or hallucinations.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The user of AI should endeavor to validate the accuracy of created content with trusted first party sources and monitor the reliability of that content. Users are accountable for their use of content created by AI and should be wary of misinformation or "hallucinations" by AI tools (e.g., citations to publications or source materials that do not exist or references that otherwise distort the truth).
evidence.snippetLocation: General Guidance for Penn Community > Accountability section

attribution.citationTitle: Statement on Guidance for the University of Pennsylvania Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
attribution.sourceRights: Tracker metadata is open licensed. Official source documents, page text, PDFs, and other source materials retain their original rights and terms.

claims.claimText: Penn users should not input moderate or high-risk Penn data (per the Penn Data Risk Classification) or intellectual property into AI tools without careful consideration of data use policies, a protective contract, and review by Penn's Privacy Office and Office of Information Security.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Users of AI should avoid sharing personal or sensitive data with the tool and should not input moderate or high-risk Penn data as defined by the Penn Data Risk Classification, or intellectual property, without: Careful consideration and understanding of the tool's use of Penn data and the service provider's stated rights to the data, including, but not limited to whether the service provider offers the option to opt-out of using customer's data to train the AI; A contract in place to protect Penn data; and Review by Penn's Privacy Office and consultation with the Office of Information Security as coordinated by Procurement when moderate or high-risk data is involved.
evidence.snippetLocation: General Guidance for Penn Community > Privacy & Contracts section

attribution.citationTitle: Statement on Guidance for the University of Pennsylvania Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
attribution.sourceRights: Tracker metadata is open licensed. Official source documents, page text, PDFs, and other source materials retain their original rights and terms.

claims.claimText: It is not permissible under HIPAA or Penn Medicine policy to share patient or research participant information with open or public AI tools and services such as ChatGPT; individual patient data and data sets (even if deidentified) may not be exposed to such tools absent institutional approval.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: It is not permissible under the Health Information Portability & Accountability Act (HIPAA) or Penn Medicine policy to share patient or research participant information in connection with open or public AI tools and services, such as ChatGPT. This is because, as currently configured, such open or public tools and services can use and share any data without regard to HIPAA restrictions and other protections. Therefore, individual patient data and patient data sets (even if deidentified) may not be exposed to open or public AI tools or services, absent institutional approval.
evidence.snippetLocation: General Guidance for Penn Community > Patient Privacy Protection section

claims.claimText: Penn’s Center for Excellence in Teaching, Learning and Innovation (CETLI) maintains updated institutional guidance on Penn-licensed AI tools, providing community access to PennChat (with free daily token allotments for FERPA-protected educational records and HIPAA-protected health information via PennKey while on campus or VPN), alongside Anthropic Enterprise (Claude), Articulate AI Assistant, Adobe Express, and Copilot Chat, while mandating that instructors must not require students to enter personal information or intellectual property into unlicensed tools.
claims.claimValue: Penn provides institutional access to licensed AI tools including PennChat, Anthropic Enterprise, and Copilot Chat for FERPA/HIPAA data, while prohibiting mandatory student entry of personal info or IP into unlicensed tools.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Penn offers access to a number of AI tools. While these Penn-licensed tools provide some added privacy protections, it is important to be aware of which tools are acceptable to use for different types of student data. ... PennChat: Free daily token allotment; •FERPA-protected educational records •HIPAA-protected health information; Log in with PennKey while on campus or connected to VPN ... Do not require students to enter personal information or intellectual property into an unlicensed AI tool.
evidence.snippetLocation: Penn-Licensed AI Tools and Publicly Available AI Tools sections

claims.claimText: Penn's Center for Excellence in Teaching, Learning and Innovation (CETLI) instructs faculty that in all cases they should not upload student work into AI detectors, stating that uploading student work without consent violates FERPA and Penn privacy policies, and noting that AI detectors are not accurate enough to serve as evidence of misconduct due to frequent bias.
claims.claimValue: Penn CETLI instructs instructors not to upload student work into AI detectors, citing FERPA, Penn privacy policies, unreliability, and bias.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: In all cases, you should not upload the student’s work into an “AI detector.” Uploading a student’s work without their consent is a violation of FERPA and Penn’s privacy policies. These tools are also not accurate enough to be treated as evidence of misconduct as they exhibit frequent bias.
evidence.snippetLocation: Frequently Asked Questions, What should I do if I suspect a student has misused AI?

claims.claimText: Penn researchers should obtain IRB approvals prior to exposing research participant data to AI tools and should exercise caution when research involves high-risk data including PII and health information.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Researchers should adhere to federal or international requirements on obtaining informed consent, and Institutional Review Board approvals should be obtained prior to exposing research participant data to AI tools. Caution should be adopted when research involves the examination of high-risk data, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and research participant health information (both identifiable and non-identifiable) exposed to AI.
evidence.snippetLocation: Additional Guidance > Guidance for Researchers section

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Do not enter any information that could identify a student. This includes names, ID numbers, or email addresses, as well as detailed descriptions of student work or engagement in class that could be identifiable to others.

claims.claimText: Wharton Academy permits students to use generative AI for brainstorming, learning efficiency, getting prompts, exploring different perspectives, asking for templates, getting preliminary feedback on written work, and language translation, at the discretion of faculty and instructional teams.
